insights.title: 1250 kVA Shore Power Autotransformer for CCG AOPS

insight.linkedin_hook: ⚡ Enabling the Arctic and Offshore Patrol Ships (AOPS): The Canadian Coast Guard is looking for a custom 1250 kVA shore power autotransformer.
insight.strategic_value:
* Marine electrification and federal greening initiatives are driving demand for shore-to-ship power conversion. DND shore facilities utilize 450 VAC, while the new CCG AOPS vessels require 600 VAC, representing a critical interoperability gap.
* The technical target is a CSA-approved, three-phase, 1250 kVA autotransformer (450V primary to 600V secondary) featuring copper windings, a CSA Type 3R enclosure, and a strict physical footprint restriction to fit inside an ISO 668 Type 1C 20-foot freight container.
* **Consulting Pivot:** Propose a physical systems integration study to the primary contact (Sarah Boyce, DND) showing how your team can pre-integrate the transformer with automated switchgear and climate controls directly inside the 20-foot ISO container before shipping, minimizing on-site commissioning costs.
insight.co_bidding_opportunity: Under the public procurement guidelines, a valid project consortium would require an electrical manufacturing contractor (such as a custom transformer builder) partnering with a marine engineering firm or a containerized power systems integrator to package and qualify the enclosure.
insight.mets_rationalization: This tender bridges Canadian Coast Guard (CCG) operations with Department of National Defence (DND) shore facilities, focusing on vessel interoperability and electrical infrastructure deployment.
